subject: Sealing the MAP: capacity reservation, lead times & GPU sizing for ClearLeaf
messages:
From: Andrew Hsu <andrew@clearleaf.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearleaf.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity planning — MAP + lead times for Dedicated/Private

Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move forward with a MAP that covers: evaluation milestones, acceptance criteria, and a firm path to reserve capacity (Dedicated or Private). A few asks to help our procurement/legal:

- Explicit lead times for Dedicated capacity tranches and for Private (on-prem) procurement.
- An initial GPU pool sizing recommendation for our pilot (estimate: 150M tokens/day, real-time chat SLA 200ms p95).
- Acceptance and rollback criteria for canary and full cutover.
- Backup plan if hardware tranche is delayed (we rely on the hosted API as fallback?).

If you can send a draft MAP and capacity model this week we can loop Legal/Procurement. Also include any gating items (SOC2 artifacts, IP/data residency notes).

Appreciate it —
Andrew Hsu
CTO, ClearLeaf Diagnostics
[attachment: brief-demo-recording.mp4 (video)]

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Hsu <andrew@clearleaf.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning — MAP + lead times for Dedicated/Private

Andrew —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is a working MAP draft and a linked capacity model (spreadsheet) with three sizing scenarios (pilot / scale / steady-state). High level summary here so Legal/Procurement can see the timing:

- Lead times
  - Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): typical procurement to handover = 6–10 weeks after contract signature for first tranche, then 3–4 weeks for subsequent tranches (depends on region and SKU).
  - Private (VPC/on-prem): 10–14 weeks for on-prem packaging + customer acceptance; if using our VPC appliance it's ~8–12 weeks.

- Sizing recommendation (starting point)
  - Pilot: 8x A100/H100-equivalent vCPU slots (estimated 60–80 TFLOPs total), mapped in the spreadsheet "capacity-model.xlsx"; target ~150M tokens/day with 200ms p95 target will be comfortable at this size with prefix caching.
  - Scale: add 2 tranches of 8 GPUs each, phased across 8–10 weeks.

- Acceptance criteria
  - Canary (week 1): 72-hour soak at 50% traffic with <2% failure rate and p95 < 250ms.
  - Full cutover: 14-day SLA observation window, regression tests (prompt set) pass at quality threshold.

- Fallbacks
  - Hosted API fallback with auto-routing policy; cost uplift documented in MAP.
  - If hardware tranche slips >2 weeks we enable temporary bursting to Hosted with cached prefixes to limit latency and cost.

Attachments: MAP-draft-CLD-v1.pdf, capacity-model.xlsx, SOC2 evidence stub included for gating.

Next steps: Ben will scope commercial tiers and Karthik + Irene will validate the sizing numbers against your prompt mix. Ben — can you propose a pricing anchor we can present to ClearLeaf Procurement?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior GTM Manager — Redwood Inference
[attachment: MAP-draft-CLD-v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Andrew Hsu <andrew@clearleaf.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning — MAP + lead times for Dedicated/Private

Andrew / team —

I've sketched a commercial anchor in the MAP PDF (tab 2) and a three-tranche commitment that aligns with the sizing Tessa proposed. Key commercial notes:

- Bridge tranche: 6-week bridge option at a slightly elevated rate to secure first-phase capacity quickly (we can hold capacity while the longer Dedicated/Private SKU order completes).
- Pricing tiers by commit: Pilot (month-to-month), Mid (6–12 month reserved at 15% discount), Full (12–36 month reserved at 25% discount).
- DocuSign: I'll prepare a mutually agreeable SOW + reservation exhibit; expecting procurement to want an exhibit that lists SKUs, tranches, and acceptance gates.

Procurement ask: please confirm whether ClearLeaf requires PO-first or signature-first for the anchor tranche — that will determine when we push the first purchase order into the queue.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[attachment: commercial-anchor.csv (spreadsheet stub)]

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Andrew Hsu <andrew@clearleaf.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning — MAP + lead times for Dedicated/Private

Andrew — quick technical points from infra/serving:

- Lead-time caveat: the 6–10 week window for Dedicated assumes SKU availability in the target region. For H100-class inventory, add a potential 2–3 week variance in Q3 due to supplier lead times.

- Sizing assumptions in the sheet:
  - We assumed average prompt length 60 tokens and 1.2 prompts/user/day. If your clinical workloads push prompt length or retrieval fan-out higher, you should expect a 30–50% increase in GPU needs.
  - We accounted for prefix/KV caching to optimize cost; if you cannot use prefix caching due to privacy/patient-data constraints we need 1.4x the pilot pool.

- Performance mitigations to reduce pool size/cost:
  - Quantization to 4-bit where acceptable (we can run evals on your eval set).
  - Batch sizing and dynamic batching policies tuned to your traffic shape.

- SOC2 & evidence: the attached stub covers logs and controls we can expose; full evidence takes legal-led access. Plan to enable audit logs during the canary window.

If you want, Karthik and I can run a quick sensitivity run against three sample prompt types next week and update the spreadsheet — that'll give you a tighter commit.

Irene Choi
Director, Inference Engineering
Redwood Inference
[attachment: soc2-evidence-stub.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Re: Capacity planning — MAP + lead times for Dedicated/Private

Team —

Thanks, this is exactly what procurement wanted to see. Two quick asks before we route to Legal:

1) One-page MAP summary that calls out the 6–10 week and 10–14 week lead-times and the bridge-tranche process we discussed (so Legal has a single-page exhibit).
2) A final prompt-sensitivity check (Irene/Karthik) — we'll provide 3 canonical prompts and a sample traffic curve.

If you can send the one-pager and a version of the spreadsheet with the sensitivity run by Monday morning we should be able to turn this to Legal next week.

Andrew
CTO, ClearLeaf Diagnostics
